subject: MAP: RidgeBank security gateplaybook and signoff asks
messages:
From: Elena Costa <elena.costa@ridgebank.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Ortega <s.ortega@ridgebank.com>, legal@ridgebank.com
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RidgeBank MAP draft + initial gating questions

Hi Neha / Jordan —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. As discussed, attached is a first-pass MAP (RidgeBank_MAP_v0.9.xlsx) that combines our timeline with the security gates RidgeBank needs to clear to reach procurement signoff. High-level asks from our side:

- Confirm SOC 2 scope and whether Redwood can provide the latest SOC 2 type II report (or an interim summary).
- SIG/CAIQ: we need a completed self-assessment and any open controls planned as part of the onboarding sprint.
- DPA: our legal team flagged two data residency carveouts and a 30-day deletion SLA for non-production logs — please confirm feasibility.
- Evidence cadence: can Redwood stage artifacts into a shared Drive folder for review (we prefer incremental access rather than a single bulk drop).

Can you confirm approximate dates for the MAP milestones? We're targeting contract execution by the end of Q2 but need the security gate verified by mid-May to make that workable.

Attachments: RidgeBank_MAP_v0.9.xlsx

Thanks,
Elena Costa
Senior Product Security Manager
RidgeBank

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Elena Costa <elena.costa@ridgebank.com>, Sam Ortega <s.ortega@ridgebank.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RidgeBank MAP draft + initial gating questions

Elena — thanks for the MAP and the clear asks. Quick answers and proposed next steps below.

1) SOC 2: we can provide the latest SOC 2 type II report (Q4 2025). I will share a redacted copy to a secure Drive folder and list the subservice auditors.

2) SIG/CAIQ: we maintain a canonical CAIQ export and will complete the customer-facing self-assessment by 3/19. For controls we do not meet, we will surface compensating controls and an implementation plan.

3) DPA + retention: the 30-day deletion SLA for non-production logs is feasible in most cases; a few audit logs are retained longer for security investigations. We propose a carveout table in section 4 of the MAP workbook to enumerate exceptions — Jordan and Kimberly are copied to advise on carveouts and redlines.

4) Evidence cadence: agreed — we can stage artifacts incrementally. Proposed cadence: weekly evidence drops (Wednesdays) starting 3/18, with a living index (sheet in the MAP workbook) linking each artifact to a gate.

Proposed MAP milestone dates (draft):
- 3/18: CAIQ export + SOC2 redacted deposit
- 4/01: DPA redline exchange (legal-to-legal)
- 4/15: Evidence sprint complete (primary gate)
- 5/08: Security acceptance signoff (final gate)
- 5/22: Executive approval and contract routing

I attached a small SOC2-Scope-Snapshot and I'll upload the MAP workbook with a colored milestone column so RidgeBank can mark priority items.

Questions for you: is the procurement window hard (end of Q2), or do you have flexibility for a short extension if an evidence item slips?

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Attachment: SOC2-Scope-Snapshot.pdf

From: Elena Costa <elena.costa@ridgebank.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Ortega <s.ortega@ridgebank.com>, legal@ridgebank.com
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RidgeBank MAP draft + initial gating questions

On Thu, Mar 5, 2026 at 11:05 AM neha_kapoor@redwood.ai wrote:
> Elena — thanks for the MAP and the clear asks. Quick answers and proposed next steps below.

Thanks Neha — this is helpful and much appreciated. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- The procurement deadline is fairly firm — our internal board wants contracts signed by 6/30, but security acceptance needs to be captured in a way that allows legal to proceed with signature routing. Mid-May signoff is ideal.
- Regarding logs: for RidgeBank non-production systems we can accept a 90-day accessible window if you can provide an audit trail for delete actions. The 30-day deletion SLA would be preferable but is not mandatory if you can't guarantee it across all pipelines.
- Can Redwood provide a brief statement about encryption-in-flight for KV cache persistence? Our infra team will want to verify technical controls.

We'll review the SOC2 snapshot and the map workbook this week. I'll route the MAP to procurement for alignment once we have the DPA redlines.

Best,
Elena

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Elena Costa <elena.costa@ridgebank.com>, Sam Ortega <s.ortega@ridgebank.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RidgeBank MAP draft + initial gating questions

Elena — quick technical add from our side and a proposal to keep the acceptance runway tight.

- Encryption: Redwood encrypts customer data in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at-rest with per-tenant keys managed via our KMS integration. KV cache persistence used for inference is stored in ephemeral volumes on private subnets; persistent caches used for model warmup are encrypted and access-controlled. I will prepare a one-page technical note and upload it to the evidence folder by 3/13.

- Logs and retention: we can offer a 30-day deletion SLA for non-production logs if RidgeBank can accept the following: (a) a 14-day hold for security incident triage before irreversible deletion; (b) a documented delete audit shipped to your audit bucket. If acceptable, we will add the carveout to the MAP workbook.

- Proposed acceptance flow to meet your mid-May target:
  1) 3/18–4/15: Evidence sprint (weekly drops)
  2) 4/16–4/24: Intake triage and control clarifications (Redwood/Security)
  3) 4/27–5/08: Joint acceptance window — RidgeBank runs validation checks
  4) 5/11: Final signoff meeting (if no critical gaps)

Also adding a small canary plan: we can run a two-week private pilot on dedicated infra with a capped request volume to validate production telemetry and retention behavior. That pilot can be a gate in the MAP and accelerate your ops team's confidence.

I'll post the tech note and a pilot runbook link to the MAP workbook. HubSpot: RB-2026-0042 will reflect the updated MAP progress.

—Jordan Blake
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Legal Team <legal@ridgebank.com>, Elena Costa <elena.costa@ridgebank.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: RidgeBank MAP draft + initial gating questions / DPA redline

Forwarding draft DPA redline for legal review — attaching DPA_Redline_Redwood_v1.docx. Key items of note:

- Section 5.2 (Data retention): added a table that enumerates retention windows and the proposed 30-day deletion SLA for non-prod logs with the 14-day hold carveout for security triage.
- Section 7 (Encryption and key management): clarifies KMS integrations and customer key options; we can scope HSM escrow if RidgeBank requires.
- Section 12 (Subprocessors): included our current subprocessors and the standard notification process for changes.

Elena / RidgeBank legal — please redline and return by 3/26 so we can honor the evidence sprint schedule. If there are material changes to the deletion SLA or residency carveouts, flag those in the DPA so we can update the MAP workbook.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Attachment: DPA_Redline_Redwood_v1.docx
